This is an important development as it results in Nvidia’s revenue being more resilient as hyperscalers shift capex toward designing and deploying their own custom chips.

The current implosion in so many stocks isn’t necessarily because their earnings are terrible. It’s because of how the market is reacting to and interpreting those earnings.

All of this reflects a shift in sentiment of the market participants, not some seismic shift in the fundamentals over the last few months.

Was sentiment far too euphoric back then? Or is the current sentiment far too bearish?

No idea and it’s not my job to know. Only time will tell.

My job is to recognize these shifts in sentiment through price action and technicals, and position myself to ride them.

Whether the market is being rational or irrational, I want to be on the right side of the move. 

I’ve been tweeting about this bearish shift in sentiment since July 2nd. July 2nd was when the $DRAM names cracked hard and broke the MA… that was the pivotal day when sentiment shifted and the euphoric trend higher in AI cracked.

name: Shay Boloor
zh_summary: StockSavvyShay argues a dislocation: $GOOGL and $AMZN plan even more AI infrastructure spend in 2027 while the market punishes check-writers; he sees the infrastructure cycle continuing and plans to keep adding high-conviction AI power, inference and agentic names.
en_summary: StockSavvyShay argues a dislocation: $GOOGL and $AMZN plan even more AI infrastructure spend in 2027 while the market punishes check-writers; he sees the infrastructure cycle continuing and plans to keep adding high-conviction AI power, inference and agentic names.
text:
I personally think there's a pretty significant dislocation happening in market right now and this week gave me some of clearest evidence yet.

Both $GOOGL and $AMZN are planning to spend even more on AI infrastructure in 2027 after already investing record amounts this year with Andy Jassy even calling AI “a once in a lifetime opportunity” and making it clear Amazon has no plans to slow down.

Putting my corporate strategy hat back on I think market is overlooking something pretty important about Google because it can no longer simply decide AI is getting too expensive and go back to its traditional Search business when AI is now threatening very product that generates most of its profits.

That means infrastructure spending is becoming just as much about defending its existing business as capturing new growth which makes these investments much harder to pull back on even if investors become increasingly concerned about returns.

And that's what makes this selloff so interesting because market is punishing the companies writing the checks while those same companies are telling us they'll write even bigger ones next year.

I absolutely expect next phase of AI to become more selective with clear winners and losers but I don't think that means the infrastructure cycle is ending which is why I plan to keep adding to my highest conviction names across AI power, AI inference and Agentic AI.

$AMZN + $GOOGL reported and their stocks sold off hard.

Neither is slowing the AI build.

Alphabet maintained its $195–205B 2026 capex guide and said spending will rise "significantly" in 2027. Cloud revenue more than doubled.

Amazon held its ~$220B 2026 capex guide and Jassy said they will spend “meaningfully more” next year. AWS grew 39%  (fastest in nearly five years) with 40%+ growth guided for 2027 and 2028.

The market is reacting to a Search miss at Google and sluggish ecommerce growth at Amazon; and to cash burn, not to a slowdown in AI infrastructure demand.

The people building the capacity are still accelerating. The market is focused on the near-term bill. That gap is the opportunity.
